meta.tagline: Portland general contractor since 1996 · save-the-client diagnosis
meta.focus: Maps grid recovery + on-page rebuild · service pages, schema, suburb-URL repair, tracking
meta.data_window: Local Dominator scans Mar 5 – May 31 2026 (169-cell grid · 7 queries · 34 files) + live site crawl 2026-06-01

tldr: On the two queries CM&D used to rank on — construction management and construction design — top-3 grid coverage has collapsed: 157 → 2 cells and 103 → 24 cells respectively between March 5 and May 31. On the four service-intent queries we track — bathroom remodel · bathroom remodeling near me · walk-in shower conversion · kitchen repair — and on contractor near me, CM&D does not appear in the top 20 in a single one of 169 grid cells. Not once. The site has one service page (/kitchen-remodeling), nine generic suburb pages with spam-pattern URLs (/dependable-..., /efficient-..., /trusted-...), zero schema markup on any page we inspected, and no GA4/GTM/Clarity tracking installed. The /bathrooms page is a 65-word portfolio gallery with no H1. There is no bathroom-remodeling, no walk-in-shower-conversion, no kitchen-repair page — yet those are the GBP services that should be driving Maps relevance. Recovery is a service-page rebuild + schema + matrix repair, in that order.

headline.h2: Two brand-name queries collapsing · five service-intent queries at zero · the site cannot back the GBP
headline.lede: The two Maps queries CM&D used to rank on are both falling fast (-155 top-3 cells on "construction management," -79 on "construction design" in 12 weeks). The four service-intent queries the GBP is configured for (bathroom remodel, walk-in shower, kitchen repair, contractor-near-me) have always been at zero — because the site has no service pages to back them. Schema is absent everywhere. Tracking is uninstalled. The recovery path is on-page + technical, fully within 90 days, with no review or PR-link spend.

root_cause.intro: Five structural gaps. A1 and A2 are why CM&D is not ranking. A3 is why the gap is widening fast. A4 is why we can't see the impact. A5 is context (out of scope but worth flagging).

items.title: The site does not back the GBP
items.body: The GBP lists 27 service items across 6 categories (Construction company · Home builder · Kitchen Renovator · Bathroom Renovator · General Contractor · Custom home builder). The site backs one of them: /kitchen-remodeling. For every other claim, when Google looks for confirming relevance signals on the site, it finds either a portfolio gallery (/bathrooms is 65 words with no H1) or nothing.

items.title: Suburb pages signal "generated content"
items.body: The nine suburb pages on the site use one of eight rotating modifiers in the URL — dependable / efficient / trusted / fast / quality (×2) / premium / local / skilled — in front of a generic service stem ("-general-contractor" or "-general-contracting-services") with "-or" suffix. The content itself is not thin (the Marylhurst page is ~950 words with specific landmarks), but the URL pattern reads as algorithmically generated, which is a known suppression trigger.

items.title: Zero schema markup anywhere
items.body: Homepage, the one service page, suburb pages, hub page — none carry LocalBusiness / GeneralContractor / Service / AreaServed JSON-LD. The Wix theme is not emitting schema and no custom code is injected. Competitors with 1-2 reviews (TS Construction, Northwest Construction, T&M Design) out-rank CM&D on the brand-name queries largely because their site/profile coupling is cleaner.

items.title: No conversion tracking installed
items.body: No Google Tag Manager, no GA4, no Microsoft Clarity, no Meta Pixel detected on the homepage. The GBP website link is correctly UTM-tagged (utm_source=google&utm_medium=organic&utm_campaign=gbp), so a gmb_click event would fire if GA4 were listening — nothing is listening. Anything we recover on rankings cannot be measured in leads, calls, or revenue until tracking is installed.

items.title: Review profile below the floor of the local pack
items.body: CM&D holds 6 reviews at 5.0★. Across the top-10 competitors on these queries, the median is 26 reviews and the leader (NW Tub & Shower) carries 841. Review work is outside HQDM scope — flagging as context so the client understands where the velocity gap is. At 6 reviews CM&D is below the threshold where review count starts contributing positively to ranking weight.

grid.intro: 13×13 grid (169 cells, 1-mile spacing) centered at (45.3642, -122.6484) — Milwaukie/Oak Grove, anchoring south Portland metro through Lake Oswego, West Linn, Oregon City and Tigard. This is exactly CM&D's GBP service area.
grid.weak_quadrant: Cells where CM&D falls fastest cluster in the northwest quadrant of the grid — the Beaverton / Tigard / Lake Oswego corridor (lat 45.38-45.45, lng -122.77 to -122.67). These are the highest-population cells; they pull more competitive results from established names. CM&D's centroid strength holds in the South Milwaukie / Oak Grove ring closer to the geocoded service area, then decays sharply toward population centers — the classic prominence/proximity signature of a profile with authority gaps.

competitors.intro: Top-10 by total top-3 cells held across the 7 tracked queries during the data window.

two_groups.label: Name-match competitors (CM&D's mirror image)
two_groups.story: 1-2 reviews each. They hold ground on the brand-name queries by literal string match — same mechanism CM&D used to. They are fragile in the same way and not the long-term threat. We beat them with the site/profile coupling they also lack.

two_groups.label: Service-specialist competitors (long-term threat)
two_groups.story: Categorize specifically (Bathroom remodeler · Architectural designer · Remodeler · General contractor) and have built review counts of 15-841. They own the service-intent grid entirely. NW Tub & Shower alone holds 3,590 top-3 cells. We don't displace NW Tub & Shower this quarter — we claim our share of Lake Oswego / West Linn / Oregon City sub-cells.

review_gap.context_note: Review work is outside HQDM scope. Surfaced as context so the AM team and client understand the velocity gap they own.

site_audit.intro: Crawl performed 2026-06-01 via WebFetch. CMS = Wix. 22 total URLs in the public sitemap.
red_flags: Only ONE service page (/kitchen-remodeling). No /bathroom-remodeling/, no /walk-in-shower-conversion/, no /kitchen-repair/, no /general-contractor/.

Nine suburb URLs use spam-pattern modifier prefixes (dependable / efficient / trusted / fast / quality ×2 / premium / local / skilled). The underlying copy is not thin but the URL cluster reads as generated.
Zero schema markup on every page sampled (homepage, /kitchen-remodeling, /quality-general-contractor-in-marylhurst-or, /serving-all-of-portland-or).
No GTM / GA4 / Clarity / Meta Pixel detected. Conversion tracking is uninstalled.
/bathrooms is a 65-word portfolio gallery with no H1.
salvageable: Marylhurst suburb page is ~950 words with specific local references (Arbor and Robinwood Creeks, Highway 43, Marylhurst Heights Park, 1950s housing stock, West Linn permits). Other suburb pages likely similar. Content survives the URL migration.
/serving-all-of-portland-or hub is ~3,200 words with neighborhood/zip/school detail. Keep as a hub.
/kitchen-remodeling is ~1,850 words. Add schema + FAQ + service-area block, otherwise leave.
GBP service items are well-structured and one-to-one match the site pages we need to build.

plan.intro: Five workstreams. D1 and D2 unlock the rest.

workstreams.title: Service-page rebuild — the core fix
workstreams.body: Build the service pages the GBP claims and the site does not back. Order: P0 = /bathroom-remodeling/ + /walk-in-shower-conversion/ + /kitchen-repair/. P1 = /kitchen-remodeling/ rebuild + /general-contractor/. P2 = /fireplace-builder/, /outdoor-living-spaces/, /insurance-rebuild/, /home-addition/. Page spec: 1,200-1,500 words, Service + AreaServed schema, suburbs-served block linking to suburb pages, FAQ (5-7 Qs), click-to-call CTA above the fold, email CTA at the end. Mirror the Marylhurst page voice — landmarks + permits — it works.
workstreams.cadence: 1-2/month. June: bathroom-remodeling + walk-in-shower-conversion. July: kitchen-repair + kitchen-remodeling rebuild. August: general-contractor + one P2.

workstreams.title: Schema — LocalBusiness + Service + AreaServed
workstreams.body: Inject JSON-LD via Wix custom code (Settings → Custom Code → Head). GeneralContractor (LocalBusiness subtype) on every page with name, phone, URL, CCB #112648, WA #CONSTMD742DF, geoCircle service area + areaServed list of the 8 anchor cities. Service schema per service page, linking provider to the GeneralContractor entity. BreadcrumbList on every non-home page. Validate via validator.schema.org and Rich Results Test.

workstreams.title: Suburb-page repair — keep content, fix URLs
workstreams.body: Rename each suburb URL from /modifier-general-contractor-in-suburb-or to /suburb/ (e.g. /marylhurst/, /west-linn/, /willamette/, /lake-oswego/, /oregon-city/, /tigard/, /milwaukie/, /beaverton/). 301 redirects from old URLs. Refresh title tag + H1 to drop the junk modifier. Keep body copy. Once D1 ships, add service-suffix children: /marylhurst/bathroom-remodeling/, /west-linn/kitchen-remodeling/, etc. — the service × suburb matrix.
workstreams.cadence: Month 1: URL migration + 301s. Months 2-3: 3 suburb refreshes/month + matrix children as their parent service pages land.

workstreams.title: Tracking + measurement install
workstreams.body: Install GTM container site-wide via Wix Marketing Tools. Deploy GA4 base tag + the four-event model: form_submit (forwards once contact form is added), contact_form_submit, click_phone_number (tel: clicks), gmb_click (utm_campaign=gbp landings). Fire Microsoft Clarity for session replay. Validate in GA4 DebugView before going live.

workstreams.title: GBP — tight surface, no review/photo/Q&A work
workstreams.body: Reviews, Q&A, photos are out of HQDM scope. Inside what we control: (a) link each GBP service item to its new site page via per-item "Learn more" once D1 lands. (b) Primary-category test in August (one 30-day swap to Home builder or Kitchen Renovator) after schema and pages have settled into index — don't move it sooner. (c) Service items + description + secondary categories are already strong; no change.
workstreams.cadence: M1: items linked through. M3: primary-category test.

quick_wins_june: Schema deployment (JSON-LD via Wix head injection) · D2
9 suburb URLs migrated to clean /suburb/ slugs + 301s in place · D3
midterm_jul_aug: Suburb refresh cadence (3/month) + matrix children on P0 services · D3
GBP service items linked to new site pages · D5
Blog program kicks off (5/month) — informational queries supporting the new services ("walk-in shower conversion cost Portland", etc.)
GBP primary-category test (30 days, August) · D5
longer_term_q4: Full service × suburb matrix completion (P0 services × 8 anchor suburbs)
Platform-migration evaluation (Wix → Webflow/Astro) — quote out before year-end. Wix is functional but caps future schema + speed work.
